feed.title: Programming Languages — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Ammonite
entry.summary: An advanced REPL that makes Scala usable for BASH-like filesystem operations.

entry.title: Awesome asyncio
entry.summary: A list of libraries and resources for asynchronous I/O in Python 3 (asyncio). Unlike general Python lists, it gathers only event-loop-friendly libraries — web frameworks, database drivers, test tools.

entry.title: Awesome C++
entry.summary: A list organising C++ libraries and frameworks by topic. Unlike general search it is a maintained, categorised starting map.

entry.title: Awesome CMake
entry.summary: A list of scripts, modules and resources for CMake, the C/C++ build tool. Unlike the official docs, it picks guides to target-based “modern CMake” practice and ready-made modules.

entry.title: Awesome Common Lisp
entry.summary: A list gathering Common Lisp libraries and tools. Unlike browsing the Quicklisp repository one by one, it groups them by domain — web, databases, GUI.

entry.title: Awesome Composer
entry.summary: A list of plugins, tools and guides for Composer, the PHP package manager. Unlike Packagist, it collects not packages but tools that extend Composer itself and improve the workflow.

entry.title: Awesome Coq
entry.summary: A list of libraries, tools and tutorials for Coq (now renamed Rocq), the formal-proof language and environment. Unlike general proof-assistant lists, it covers only the Coq ecosystem.

entry.title: Awesome Elixir
entry.summary: A library list for the Elixir language and Erlang ecosystem. Unlike a Hex package search it is curated and grouped by topic.

entry.title: Awesome Python Scientific Audio
entry.summary: A list of Python libraries for scientific research in audio/music. Unlike general audio tools it is research-oriented: feature extraction, music information retrieval, source separation.

entry.title: Awesome Python Typing
entry.summary: A list of tools and resources for optional static typing in Python. Unlike the mypy docs, it brings together type checkers (mypy, Pyright, Pyre), stub packages and runtime validators.

entry.title: Awesome Ruby
entry.summary: A list gathering Ruby libraries and tools category by category. Unlike a RubyGems search it is curated, current and grouped.

entry.title: Awesome Rust
entry.summary: A list organising Rust libraries and applications by topic. Unlike a crates.io search it is a curated, categorised and maintained starting map.

entry.title: Awesome Scala
entry.summary: A topic-by-topic list of Scala libraries and tools. Unlike scattered search it shows functional and big-data libraries together.

entry.title: Awesome V
entry.summary: A list of libraries, tools and projects for the V language. Unlike Go or Rust lists, it gathers the ecosystem of a still-young language in one place; since the language changes quickly, check how current entries are.

entry.title: better-files
entry.summary: A thin NIO wrapper library that makes file operations in Scala easy.

entry.title: C#
entry.summary: Microsoft’s general-purpose language for the .NET platform.

entry.title: Clojure
entry.summary: A modern Lisp dialect on the JVM, focused on immutability.

entry.title: Coursier
entry.summary: A fast JVM dependency resolver and application launcher written in pure Scala.

entry.title: Dart
entry.summary: Google’s client-oriented language, the one beneath Flutter.

entry.title: Elixir
entry.summary: A functional language on the Erlang VM, strong in scalability.

entry.title: Go
entry.summary: Google’s simple, fast-compiling language strong in concurrency — its official site.

entry.title: Haskell
entry.summary: A purely functional, statically typed programming language with lazy evaluation.

entry.title: JCTools
entry.summary: Very high-performance concurrent queues for the JVM, used by projects like Netty.

entry.title: JMH
entry.summary: An OpenJDK tool for microbenchmarking on the JVM that accounts for JIT effects that distort measurement. Unlike timing by hand it correctly handles traps like warmup and dead-code elimination.

entry.title: Julia
entry.summary: A high-performance open-source language for scientific computing. Unlike Python it JIT-compiles to near-C speed, aiming to remove the “two-language problem” of prototyping in Python and rewriting hot code in C.

entry.title: Julia.jl
entry.summary: A comprehensive list organising Julia packages and resources by topic. Unlike a package search, it hand-classifies packages by scientific field; some sections may be dated.

entry.title: Kotlin
entry.summary: A cross-platform language on the JVM, the preferred language for Android.

entry.title: Lua
entry.summary: A lightweight, embeddable scripting language, common in games and embedded systems.

entry.title: OpenJDK
entry.summary: The open-source reference implementation of the Java platform — where the language and JVM are developed. Unlike vendor distributions the standard itself is defined here.

entry.title: Perl
entry.summary: A dynamic, mature language strong in text processing and system scripting.

entry.title: PHP
entry.summary: One of the most common server-side languages of the web — its official docs.

entry.title: R
entry.summary: A language and environment designed for statistics and data analysis, with tens of thousands of packages on CRAN. Unlike Python, new statistical methods usually appear here first, and it has graphics tools such as ggplot2.

entry.title: Ruby
entry.summary: A multi-paradigm language foregrounding readability and developer happiness.

entry.title: Rust by Example
entry.summary: The official resource giving each concept as a runnable, editable code example. Unlike the book it cuts the prose and leads with the example — for those who learn by trying.

entry.title: Rust Playground
entry.summary: The official space to compile and run Rust code in the browser with no install. Unlike a local setup it gives compiler output and ASM/MIR via a shareable link.

entry.title: Rustlings
entry.summary: An exercise set teaching Rust by fixing small, broken snippets. Unlike reading-based resources it has you read and fix compiler errors by hand.

entry.title: Scala
entry.summary: A language on the JVM uniting object-oriented and functional programming.

entry.title: Scalastyle
entry.summary: A linter that checks Scala source against formatting and style rules.

entry.title: Scoverage
entry.summary: A statement-based code-coverage tool for Scala, more precise than line-based coverage.

entry.title: Swift
entry.summary: Apple’s safe, fast-compiled language, developed primarily for iOS.
